History:
- Patient presents with a left elbow swelling noted about one week ago, discovered incidentally in the shower.
- Swelling is painless, slightly warm, with a sensation of fluid inside.
- No known trauma or injury to the affected elbow.
- No prior episodes or similar symptoms.
- Patient works at a desk job, no heavy physical activity related to the elbow.
- Reports generally good health and regular running (2-3 times weekly).
- No associated systemic symptoms reported.

Past Medical History:
- Known diagnosis of osteoarthritis confirmed by GP several years ago.
- Allergy to peanuts.
- No known medication allergies.
- Not currently taking any regular medications.
- No other chronic illnesses reported.
- No known family history of rheumatological diseases (patient uncertain).

Physical Examination:
- Visible swelling on the left elbow, slightly warm to touch.
- Dry skin noted at the tip of the elbow; no history of eczema or other skin conditions.
- Elbow movement normal, no tenderness over the joint itself.
- Mild discomfort when pressing adjacent to the swelling.
- No signs suggestive of septic arthritis: no intense redness, severe pain, or spreading erythema.
- Patient alert, oriented, and systemically well.

Impression:
- Left elbow bursitis (inflammation of the olecranon bursa).

Management Plan:
- Initiate oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID): Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food.
- Advise to stop NSAIDs if heartburn or gastrointestinal symptoms occur.
- Arrange blood tests to include inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatological antibodies, and gout screen.
- Blood test forms to be sent to patient’s home with instructions for collection.
- Follow-up consultation (phone, video, or face-to-face) arranged after blood test results to reassess condition.
- Patient advised to seek urgent medical attention if elbow develops worsening redness, spreading erythema, increased pain, or other signs of infection.

Patient Summary:
- A 53-year-old man with known osteoarthritis presents with a painless swollen left elbow for one week, consistent with bursitis.
- No signs of infection noted currently; conservative NSAID treatment initiated.
- Blood tests to evaluate for inflammatory or rheumatological causes are arranged.
- Follow-up to be scheduled after results to guide further management.

Key Takeaways:
- Start Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food and monitor for GI side effects.
- Watch for worsening symptoms such as increasing redness, pain, or swelling that would require urgent review.
- Complete blood tests as arranged to exclude other causes of elbow swelling.

Next Steps:
- Patient to perform blood tests once forms are received.
- Follow-up appointment (telehealth or in-person) after test results to review progress and refine diagnosis.
- Patient to promptly contact healthcare provider if symptoms worsen before follow-up.

Document Quality:
- Allergies, medications, and past medical history adequately documented.
- No internal conflicts noted in the transcript.
- Transcript clear and fully understandable with minimal filler or interruptions.
